subject: Visual Art
examFormat: Three papers, all compulsory; Papers 1 and 2 are a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1 has forty multiple-choice questions in 50 minutes for 40 marks. Paper 2 has eight essay questions in three sections (A General knowledge in art; B Art of West Africa; C Pre-historic, Ancient Egyptian and Western art); candidates answer four (one from A, two from B, one from C) in 2 hours for 60 marks. Paper 3 is practical: Section A Drawing (one question, 3 hours, 100 marks), Section B Creative Design 2-D (one question, 3 hours, 100 marks) and Section C Creative Design 3-D (one question, within six months, 100 marks); May/June candidates answer A and either B or C, November/December candidates answer A and B only.
excluded: Art organisations specific to Ghana or The Gambia (Ghana Artists Association, Ghana Craftsmen Association, Ghana Arts Council, Gambia Art Teachers Association) were omitted from the list of art organisations; the reading list was skipped.

topics.name: Nature and branches of Art and careers in art
objectives: Describe the nature and branches of art and careers in art

topics.name: Art elements
objectives: Show visual awareness, understanding and appreciation of art elements, their forms, characteristics and functions, e.g. line, colour, space, shape, form, texture

topics.name: Principles of Art
objectives: Apply creatively art and design principles, e.g. balance, rhythm, proportion, harmony, emphasis, variety

topics.name: Perspective
objectives: Explain the meaning and types of perspective, e.g. aerial, linear (angular/parallel) and foreshortening

topics.name: Art and craft tools and materials
objectives: Show knowledge of the production, use and care of art/craft tools and materials, e.g. brush, pencil, colour, palette, easels

topics.name: Art and craft terms
objectives: Explain art and craft terms, e.g. tie and dye, biscuit ware, silhouette, relief, chiaroscuro, sfumato, aperture

topics.name: Inter-relationships of the arts
objectives: Explain the inter-relationships of the arts, e.g. music, visual art, dance, drama and literary arts

topics.name: Art of West Africa: general concepts
objectives: Show knowledge of traditional art of West Africa: basic concepts (e.g. animism, fetishism and mythology), art forms, geographical location, characteristics, underlying beliefs and the sacred and secular functions of art
Show general knowledge of contemporary artists and art educators, their works, style, media, materials and contribution to the development of art

topics.name: Ancient Traditional Art of West Africa
objectives: Show knowledge of the ancient traditional art of the following peoples
topics.content: Cameroon - Bamileke; Dahomey (now Benin Republic) - Fon; Gambia - Wollof, Mandinka, Jola; Ghana (formerly Gold Coast) - Ashanti, Fante, Ewe, Frafra; Guinea - Kissi; Cote d'Ivoire (Ivory Coast) - Senufo, Baule; Liberia - Dan and Ngere; Mali - Dogon, Bambara; Sierra Leone - Mende, Sherbro; Upper Volta (now Burkina Faso) - Mossi, Bobo, Kurumba; Nigeria - Benin, Ife, Nok, Igbo-Ukwu, Esie, Owo, etc.

topics.name: Modern Traditional Art of West Africa
objectives: Show knowledge of modern traditional art forms
topics.content: Oshogbo art, Ashanti and Ewe Kente, modern Benin art, Winneba pottery, Abuja pottery, Ntoso adinkra, Bida brass works, calabash carving, Enyiresi basketry, Mbari mud sculpture, weaving, leatherwork, wall decoration, indigenous decorative motifs.

subtopics.name: Art institutions, organisations and cultural festivals
objectives: Identify art institutions (art schools, art galleries, arts centres, museums) and the departments responsible for art and culture
Identify art organisations, e.g. INSEA, NSIAD, NAAC, SNA, NSEA, Ona Art Movement of Artists, Ulli Art Movement, The Eye Society
Explain the artistic significance of cultural festivals, e.g. costumes, symbols, objects, masks, body decorations, wall decorations

subtopics.name: Outstanding contemporary West African artists
objectives: Describe the training, style, achievements and contributions to the development of art of outstanding contemporary West African artists

topics.name: Pre-historic Art
objectives: Describe pre-historic (Early man's) art, 20,000-2000 BC (Paleolithic, Mesolithic and Neolithic stone ages): beliefs, materials, characteristics and functions

topics.name: Ancient Egyptian Art
objectives: Describe ancient Egyptian art (Old, Middle and New Kingdoms): beliefs, styles and functions

topics.name: Greek Art
objectives: Describe Greek art: periods (Archaic, Classical and Hellenistic), characteristics and artists

topics.name: Medieval Art
objectives: Describe medieval art: features, media and characteristics

topics.name: Renaissance Art
objectives: Describe Early, Low and High Renaissance art and artists, e.g. Giotto, Donatello, Masaccio

subtopics.name: Impressionism
objectives: Describe Impressionism and its artists: Paul Cezanne, Claude Monet, Edouard Manet, Georges Seurat

subtopics.name: Post Impressionism
objectives: Describe Post Impressionism (late 19th century) and its artists: Vincent van Gogh, Paul Gauguin, etc.

topics.name: 20th Century Art: Cubism
objectives: Describe Cubism, the influence of African art and the artists Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque

topics.name: Paper 3 Part A: Drawing
objectives: Observe, analyse and accurately depict natural and man-made objects
Represent the structure and forms of the human figure
topics.content: Works may be rendered in pencil, pastel, charcoal, pen and ink or poster/water colour. Candidates attempt one alternative only; all carry equal marks.

subtopics.name: Drawing from Objects
objectives: Observe and interpret a group of arranged man-made objects (e.g. old radio sets, parts of cars, bicycles, machines, bottles) as a total composition

subtopics.name: Drawing from Nature
objectives: Study natural objects (branch, flowers, foliage, fruits, vegetables, rocks, bones, insects, birds, shells, fish, crustacean, skeleton) to bring out the beauty of their forms and/or nature of growth

subtopics.name: Drawing from Life
objectives: Observe and depict accurately the structure and form of a living person posed in a described attitude

topics.name: Paper 3 Part B: Creative Design (2-Dimensional)
objectives: Visualize ideas and situations, and communicate personal vision with originality and imagination in 2-dimensional art forms
topics.content: Six questions: two each on graphic design, textile design and picture making; one question is attempted.

subtopics.name: Lettering and Poster Design
objectives: Design and lay out a brief notice requiring formal lettering (Roman, Gothic or other formalized characters)
Create pictorial posters with suitable lettering
Do lettering and layout for greeting cards, formal invitations, book jackets, logo types, emblems, symbols, labels, wall hangings, etc.

subtopics.name: Book Illustration
objectives: Illustrate stories and texts in books, magazines and newspapers

subtopics.name: Printmaking
objectives: Do printmaking: linocut, woodcut, yam print, stenciling, screen printing and others

subtopics.name: Package Design
objectives: Design packages, e.g. wrappers, cereal packages and record (CD) jackets

subtopics.name: Computer Graphics
objectives: Design any of the above using computer software, e.g. CorelDraw, Adobe Photoshop

subtopics.name: Textile Design
objectives: Design a piece of unsewn material at least two metres in length, dyed in a pattern as in batik or tie and dye, or printed as in block or screen printing

subtopics.name: Applique
objectives: Make applique: shaped fabric pieces sewn on a foundation fabric to form a design or pattern

subtopics.name: Tapestry
objectives: Make tapestry: a fabric with a woven pattern or picture used as wall hanging, upholstery, etc.

subtopics.name: Painting
objectives: Create illustrative compositions of ideas (themes) from everyday life or imagination using a suitable medium, including mural

subtopics.name: Photography
objectives: Demonstrate basic knowledge and creative skill in shooting and printing pictures of portraits, landscape, seascape, nature and pets
Experiment with simple photo tricks, e.g. photograms and image distortion in printing

subtopics.name: Mosaic
objectives: Make a picture with small pieces of regular-shaped coloured materials, e.g. glass, paper or tile stuck onto a surface

subtopics.name: Collage
objectives: Make a picture by synthesizing irregular-shaped materials like cloth, pieces of paper and other objects onto a surface

topics.name: Paper 3 Part C: Creative Design (3-Dimensional)
objectives: Communicate personal ideas and vision with originality and imagination in 3-dimensional art forms
topics.content: Candidates may use clay, papier-mache, wood/plywood, cement, fibre-glass, Plaster-of-Paris, paper (including embossed/texturized cardboard, chip-board and straw-board), etc. The project is executed within six months of the examination year; notes, diagrams and working drawings must be submitted with the finished project and constitute 10% of the total marks.

subtopics.name: Sculpture
objectives: Produce sculpture in clay, metal, wood, papier-mache, cement, etc. (clay works must be fired)

subtopics.name: Product Design/Modeling
objectives: Design and produce models of industrial products, such as automobiles, phones, bottles, cosmetics

subtopics.name: Ceramics
objectives: Make ceramic wares such as jugs, flower vases, bowls, moulded, hand-built or thrown on the wheel, or other objects such as a toy animal or figure (clay works must be fired)

subtopics.name: Basketry
objectives: Make mats, chairs, hats, stools, bags, macrame or other useful objects designed and woven or plaited in cane, raffia, etc.

subtopics.name: Jewellery
objectives: Design and construct ornaments with metals, beads, plastic, shells, seeds, etc.

subtopics.name: Calabash Decoration
objectives: Design and decorate calabash using various methods
